outcomes.question: Is my fee overdue, and what is the late fee?
outcomes.text:
Your fee for the Odd Semester 2026‑27 is still **unpaid**, not yet **overdue**.  
The due date was 12 September 2026, and a fee becomes “overdue” only after it has been unpaid for more than 30 days (i.e., from 13 October 2026) [1].

A late‑fee of **₹500 per week (or part of a week)** starts accruing from 13 September 2026 [2].  

From 13 September 2026 to today 4 October 2026 is 22 days, which counts as 4 weeks (any part of a week is charged).  

**Late fee accrued so far:** 4 weeks × ₹500 = **₹2,000** [2] [3].

So, the fee is not overdue yet, and the current late‑fee amount is ₹2,000.

outcomes.question: Can attendance shortage be condoned on medical grounds?
outcomes.text:
Yes. Attendance shortfalls can be condoned on medical grounds, but only if the student meets the required conditions:

* The student must have at least 65 % attendance in the course; otherwise condonation is not permitted [1].
* The medical ground must be an illness or injury that required hospitalisation, or a period of rest of three or more consecutive days, certified by a registered medical practitioner. The certificate must state the period of incapacity and be issued during the illness or within seven days of its end [2].
* The application must be made before the examination‑form window closes [3].
* A student may receive condonation in no more than two courses in a semester (and four across the whole programme) [4].

Thus, provided these criteria are satisfied, an attendance shortage can be condoned on medical grounds.

outcomes.question: What is the anti-ragging policy?
outcomes.text:
**Anti‑Ragging Policy (Odd Semester 2026‑27)**  

- Ragging in any form, on‑ or off‑campus, in hostels, transport or online, is absolutely prohibited and is a punishable offence under the University Code of Conduct, the UGC Regulations (2009) and may also violate the Indian Penal Code and the Gujarat Prohibition of Ragging Act. [1]  

- Every student (and a parent/guardian) must submit an anti‑ragging undertaking on the student portal (and the national portal) before the start of the semester; without it the student is not registered. [2]  

- The Anti‑Ragging Committee (chaired by the Vice‑Chancellor’s nominee and including faculty, staff, parents, students and police/administrative representatives) oversees all anti‑ragging measures and decides on complaints. [3]  

- The Anti‑Ragging Squad (faculty and wardens) conducts surprise visits to hostels, canteens and other common areas, especially during the first six weeks of the semester (16 June – 31 July 2026), and investigates complaints on the spot. [3]  

- Any student who is ragged or witnesses ragging may report it **round‑the‑clock** via:  
  1. University anti‑ragging helpline (toll‑free, printed on ID cards) – 1800‑000‑0000;  
  2. Online complaint form on the student portal (anonymous option);  
  3. National anti‑ragging helpline 1800‑180‑5522 or helpline@antiragging.in;  
  4. Directly to any member of the Anti‑Ragging Squad, a warden, the Dean of Student Affairs or any faculty member, who must forward the report to the Committee the same day. [4]  

- Upon a complaint, the Squad records it, ensures the victim’s safety and medical care, and reports to the Committee within 24 hours. The Committee must hear the accused student within 7 days and decide the case within 15 days; serious cases may be reported to police. [5]  

- Penalties for ragging range from suspension to expulsion and may include a police report, as specified in Part VII clause 8 of the regulations. [6]

outcomes.question: What's in Unit 3 of DBMS?
outcomes.text:
Unit 3 of the Database Management Systems course covers **Normalization and File Organization** (10 hours). Topics include:

- Importance of good schema design and problems with poor designs  
- Dependency theory: functional dependencies, Armstrong’s axioms, minimal covers  
- Normal forms: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF  
- File organization methods: sequential, indexed, random, multi‑key, hashing  
- Indexing structures, storage strategies, B‑trees and B+‑trees

outcomes.question: What is the attendance condonation rule I should tell my students?
outcomes.text:
The attendance‑condonation rule is:

* The Head of the Department may condone a shortfall in attendance and allow the student to sit the end‑semester exam, but only if the student’s attendance in that course is **at least 65 %** [1].
* A student can receive condonation for **no more than two courses in a semester** and **no more than four courses in the entire programme** [2].
* Condonation **only admits the student to the exam**; it does **not change the recorded attendance percentage** and it is **not a defence in any later disciplinary proceeding** [3].
* The authority to grant condonation rests with the **Head of the Department offering the course**, subject to the limits above [4].

outcomes.question: What is the late-fee rule for overdue payments?
outcomes.text:
A fee that is not paid in full by the due date incurs a **late fee of ₹500 for each week (or any part of a week) the payment is delayed**, starting the day after the due date and continuing until the fee is paid [1].  

When the fee remains unpaid more than 30 days after the due date (i.e., becomes “overdue”), the same ₹500‑per‑week (or part‑week) charge continues to apply [2] [3].
